translation: Sweetheart... sweetheart... hey, sweetheart...
There you go again, what is it, girl? You keep coming all the time and spoiling my work.. ruining my business...
Oho, look at the dandy.. come and see his mighty grand business.. enough, enough, sweetheart...
Hey.. what is it.. ah..
My business will go to ruin, girl
Your carry-on is getting too ripe, girl
My business will go to ruin, girl
Your carry-on is getting too ripe, girl
If it's ruined, let it be ruined, boy
My carry-on is still tender, lad
If it's ruined, let it be ruined, boy
My carry-on is still tender, lad
Time and again you spoil things with your talk
And you ripen my heart with just your glances
Time and again you spoil things with your talk
And you ripen my heart with just your glances
When I try to catch you, you run away
When I talk of marrying you, you slip away
When I try to catch you, you run away
When I talk of marrying you, you slip away
Have you ever once bought me red bangles?
Have you ever brought me even one Bandarulanka sari?
Have you ever once bought me red bangles?
Have you ever brought me even one Bandarulanka sari?
All you say is business, business
And you mock the beauty standing right in front of you
All you say is business, business
And you mock the beauty standing right in front of you
No, no, don't take it that way again. I went to the market just for you.. look how many fine bangles I bought, since they were cheap
Chhee chhee chhee chhee
You buy me thin bangles because they come cheap?
Would you gather tamarinds just because they're free?
You buy me thin bangles because they come cheap?
Would you gather tamarinds just because they're free?
You're a miser, sweetheart
How is anyone to do business with you?
You're a miser, sweetheart
How is anyone to do business with you?
Aha, don't misunderstand.. you look lovely when you wear thin bangles..
You look lovely when you wear thin bangles
Cheap or costly, I'll buy them for you
What is there in a price, o girl?
You are right here in my heart, look again
What is there in a price, o girl?
You are right here in my heart, look again
Oho.. you've learned a lot of sweet talk, sweetheart..
If I am in your heart, o sweetheart
Come, let's have all the fun we long for
Thank goodness.. you've finally understood, my dear
Let's stay with each other, o girl
Let's become one in each other, come, girl
Let's stay with each other, o girl
Let's become one in each other, come, girl
Let's pass our days laughing and frolicking
Let's go on swaying and rocking along
Let's pass our days laughing and frolicking
Let's go on swaying and rocking along
Let's pass our days laughing and frolicking
Let's go on swaying and rocking along

Let's go on swaying and rocking along
summaryEn: This lively love song is a comic quarrel between a small trader and the woman who loves him. It mixes spoken banter with sung verses. It opens with her calling 'mava' (sweetheart) and him grumbling that she keeps turning up and ruining his business. She mocks his 'grand business'. The sung part plays on two words that sound alike: vyaparam (business) and yavvaram (an affair or carry-on). He warns that his business will be ruined and her carry-on is getting 'too ripe'. She answers, let it be ruined, her carry-on is still 'tender'. She complains that he runs off when she tries to catch him, slips away at the mention of marriage, and has never bought her red bangles or a Bandarulanka sari (a local handloom sari). When he proudly shows off thin bangles he bought because they were cheap, she laughs at him with a proverb-like jab: would you gather tamarinds just because they're free? She calls him a miser. He pleads that price means nothing because she lives in his heart, and she softens. It ends with both agreeing to go through life together, laughing and swaying. Sung by Sri Hari Jagannath and Shashikala on Konaseema Janapadalu (2003).
summaryTe: ఈ ఉల్లాసమైన ప్రేమ గీతం ఒక చిన్న వ్యాపారికి, అతన్ని ప్రేమించే అమ్మాయికి మధ్య జరిగే హాస్యభరితమైన గొడవ. మాటలు, పాట కలగలిసి సాగుతుంది. ఆమె 'మావా' అని పిలవడంతో మొదలవుతుంది. అతను 'అస్తమానం వచ్చి వ్యాపారం చెడగొడతావు' అని విసుక్కుంటాడు. ఆమె అతని 'మహా గొప్ప వ్యాపారాన్ని' ఎగతాళి చేస్తుంది. పాట భాగం ఒకేలా వినిపించే రెండు పదాలతో ఆడుకుంటుంది: 'వ్యాపారం', 'యవ్వారం'. 'వ్యాపారం సెడిపోద్ది, నీ యవ్వారం ముదురుతోంది' అని అతనంటే, 'సెడిపోతే సెడిపోనీ, నా యవ్వారం లేతదే' అని ఆమె బదులిస్తుంది. పట్టుకుందామంటే పరిగెడతాడని, పెళ్ళి మాట ఎత్తితే జారిపోతాడని, ఎప్పుడూ ఎర్ర గాజులు గానీ బండారులంక చీర గానీ కొనిపెట్టలేదని ఆమె నిష్ఠూరమాడుతుంది. చౌకగా వచ్చాయని కొన్న సన్నగాజులను అతను గర్వంగా చూపిస్తే, 'ఊరకొస్తే చింతకాయలు ఏరుకొస్తావా?' అని సామెతలాంటి మాటతో ఎద్దేవా చేసి, అతన్ని పీనాసి అంటుంది. ధరలో ఏముంది, నువ్వు నా ఎదలో ఉన్నావని అతను బతిమాలడంతో ఆమె కరిగిపోతుంది. ఇద్దరూ నవ్వుతూ తుళ్ళుతూ కలిసి జీవితం సాగిద్దామని నిర్ణయించుకోవడంతో పాట ముగుస్తుంది. Konaseema Janapadalu (2003) ఆల్బమ్‌లో శ్రీహరి జగన్నాథ్, శశికళ పాడారు.
